provider.title: AI model

gemini.name: Gemini (Google)
gemini.description: Fast and cheap. A free tier exists, but it is sometimes overloaded.

anthropic.name: Claude (Anthropic)
anthropic.description: Very good reading, handwriting included. Paid, a few cents per lesson.

openai.name: OpenAI-compatible (OpenAI, OpenRouter…)
openai.description: OpenAI, or OpenRouter: one key for GPT, Claude, Gemini, Mistral… “Other” accepts any compatible service (Ollama, LM Studio…).

fake.name: Demo
fake.description: Canned cards, for tests and development.
fake.warning: Demo mode: the cards don't come from your photos, they are always the same. Choose another provider to use Cartable.

provider.modelHint: Leave empty for the default model.
provider.fallbacksHint: Tried in order when the main model is overloaded (comma-separated).

access.title: Access
access.openaiKey: Service API key (not needed for a local service)
access.replaceHint: To replace it, paste the new key.
access.willBeCleared: Will be deleted when you save.
access.ollamaHint: OpenAI-compatible service: its address usually ends with /v1 (local Ollama: http://localhost:11434/v1).
access.testOk: ✓ {model} reads images and answers in the right format ({seconds} s).

access.testRefused: ⚠ {model} doesn't accept images (“{refused}”). Pick a vision model.

voice.title: Card voices

anki.title: 📥 Send straight to Anki
anki.embedded: ✓ Cartable runs inside the Anki add-on: “Add to Anki” writes straight into the open profile, no AnkiConnect needed.
anki.howTo: To add cards without an .apkg file: in Anki on the computer, Tools → Add-ons → Get Add-ons, code 2055492159 (AnkiConnect), then restart Anki. Anki must be open while sending. Or install the Cartable add-on, which runs Cartable inside Anki.
anki.addressHint: Anki on the same computer as Cartable: http://localhost:8765.
anki.keyPlaceholder: Only if “apiKey” is set in AnkiConnect
anki.syncHint: (to get the cards on the phone)
anki.testNoProfile: Anki answers, but no profile is open: open one in Anki.
anki.syncOff: “{profile}” isn't logged in to AnkiWeb: no sync after sending. To sync, log in in Anki (Sync button).

addon.stoppedAtStart: The Cartable server stopped while starting.
addon.phoneSteps:
1. Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi as this computer.
2. Scan this QR code with the phone's camera.
3. In the browser: menu → “Add to Home screen”, to use it like an app.

Settings (AI keys…) open here, on the computer: Tools → Cartable → Settings.
addon.localOnly: ⚠ The server only listens on this computer (“host” set to 127.0.0.1): set “0.0.0.0” in the add-on config to reach it from the phone.
addon.notRunningYet: Cartable is starting: try again in a few seconds.
addon.installConfirm:
Before it can start, Cartable must install its components:

• uv (from GitHub), Python 3.13 and its Python libraries (from PyPI): about 300 MB on disk;
• only in the add-on's own folder: nothing changes on the rest of the computer, and removing the add-on removes them.

This takes a minute or two, the first time and after some updates. Install now?
addon.installDeclined: Cartable isn't started. To install it later: Tools → Cartable → Open Cartable.

auto.name: Automatic (from the lesson)

vocabulary.name: Vocabulary of a language
vocabulary.text: Create Anki cards with the vocabulary of the language lesson. One word or expression per card. Front in my language, back in the language being learned, with the article for nouns. In "info", give the gender, the plural when it is irregular, and a short example if the lesson has one.

sentences.name: Sentences of a language
sentences.text: Create Anki cards with the complete sentences of the language lesson. Front: the sentence in my language. Back: the sentence in the language being learned.

questions.name: Questions / answers
questions.text: Create question → answer cards to review the content of the lesson (dates, definitions, key ideas). Short, precise questions and brief answers, in English.

cloze.name: Fill in the blanks
cloze.text: Create cloze cards with the important sentences of the lesson: in each sentence, hide what is worth remembering (dates, names, key words), one gap per idea, three at most per sentence. Back: empty.

formulas.name: Formulas (maths, physics…)
formulas.text: Create one card per formula of the lesson. Front: what the formula calculates (or its name). Back: the formula. Info: what each letter stands for.

school_formulas.name: Middle school maths formulas
school_formulas.text: Create cards for the main maths formulas of middle school (ages 11 to 15): areas and perimeters (square, rectangle, triangle, circle), volumes (cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere), Pythagoras, Thales (intercept theorem), trigonometry (cos, sin, tan), special products, powers, proportionality and percentages, average speed. Front: what the formula calculates. Back: the formula. Info: what each letter stands for, with its unit when useful.

diagram.name: Diagram to complete
diagram.text: The photo shows a diagram with labels (names linked to the drawing by an arrow or a line). Hide the text of each label behind a number and make one card per label. Front: the diagram, with the question "What is (n)?". Back: the text of the label.

pictures.name: Words in pictures
pictures.text: Create cards with the words of the lesson (without a photo: 10 common words of the topic I add here). Front: the picture of the word, with the question "How do you say it?". Back: the word in the language being learned, with the article. Info: the word in English.

wordlist.name: Word list (no photo)
wordlist.text:
Create one card per word of the list below. Front: the word in English. Back: its translation into Spanish, with the article.
List:

dictation.name: Spelling dictation
dictation.text: Create one card per word to learn to spell, from the lesson or from the list below. Front: a short sentence using the word, with the word replaced by "…" (its definition if the sentence isn't enough to guess it). Back: the word alone, written exactly as in the sentence. Info: a useful spelling tip (silent letter, word family…), otherwise empty.
